item.title: BE ALERT - SPECIAL MARINE WATCH IN EFFECT
item.description:
Generic Warning | Special Marine Watch In Effect |

Conditions are favourable for the development of wind gusts between 45 to 55 knots in marine regions in southwestern Hudson Bay early in the morning of Sunday October 25th. Potential for significant wave heights accompanies these winds, so mariners are advised to exercise caution, especially smaller vessels. The winds are expected to lessen in severity over the course of Sunday afternoon. This watch may be expanded eastward as the event draws near. Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. For more information monitor Canadian Coast Guard radio or Weatheradio stations.

| Extreme - extraordinary threat | Future - act in near future

item.title: Corn, Soybean & Oilseed Performance Workshop - Winsloe
item.description:
Corn, Soybean & Oilseed Performance Workshop - Winsloe slmacneil Thu, 10/22/2026 - 08:53

The 2027 PEI Field Crop Performance Series will bring together trends from ACE Network field data, firsthand experiences from producers and agronomists, and insight from crop specialists. Presentations and discussions will explore what is working in the field today, as well as emerging trends and practices that could help Atlantic Canadian producers advance crop yield and quality in the future.

Come compare experiences, ask questions and take home practical ideas to consider for your farm.

Join us for the 2027 PEI Field Crop Performance Series, featuring practical ideas, farmer experiences and conversations about what is working in the field.

item.title: Premier McLeod on the Enbridge Line 21 Pipeline
item.description:
YELLOWKNIFE - Premier Bob McLeod issued the following statement on the Enbridge Line 21 pipeline today:

“I was pleased to learn that operations have resumed for Enbridge’s Line 21 pipeline after almost 2 years of no activity.

"Resource development has, and will continue to be, the backbone of our economy and is central to ensuring a good source of middle class jobs and business opportunities. Our territory has mineral and petroleum resources and the development of those resources can have a transformative effect on our people and economy.

"Sustainable economic development is key to the future of Northerners. With a strong resource development base, we will be able to support diversification of our local economies into emerging and established sectors.

"On behalf of the Government of the Northwest Territories I’d like to offer my congratulations to Imperial Oil, Enbridge the town of Norman Wells and other partners for getting this pipeline back up and running. I know the efforts and economic impacts of the pipeline have already begun to take shape in the community and will be felt for years to come. ”

 

Charlotte Digness
Media and Communications Coordinator
Cabinet Communications and Protocol
Government of the Northwest Territories
Ph: 867-767-9140 ext. 11092
Email: charlotte_digness@gov.nt.ca
